statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 15 while Stress stays elevated at 50.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Stress stays elevated on 24-year-high long-end yields and a narrow intraday recovery. A narrow caution window is flagged for the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where a delayed post-minutes second leg is the main conditional risk.
headline: NDX retraces its gap-down as the FOMC minutes land and the 10-year eases from a 24-year high
body: The Nasdaq-100 opened lower at 30,976 against a record 31,224.69 prior close, traded down to 30,904 and has since recovered to about 31,135, close to the 31,146 session high. That is a substantial completed retracement rather than a one-way path, which is the central reason Tail stays in the low band. The September 15-16 FOMC minutes, released at 14:00 ET, show all participants backing the quarter-point hike and most expecting a further increase by year end, with inflation risks seen tilted to the upside. Despite that hawkish tone the 10-year yield eased to about 5.28% after touching 5.36%, its highest since 2002, helped by a solid 39 billion dollar 10-year auction that stopped at 5.300%. VIX is near 15.15 after a 16.01 session high, so realised volatility is decaying rather than expanding. Stress stays elevated because the backdrop is genuinely difficult: long-end yields sit at multi-decade highs, Brent trades above 100 dollars with continuing tanker attacks around the Strait of Hormuz, consumer inflation expectations came in at 3.9% against a 3.7% consensus, and the recovery is narrow, with the Russell 2000 down about 1.2% and Nvidia near its session low. That conflict reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress without establishing the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures. The named risk window is the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where a delayed repricing of the minutes could combine with cash-close imbalance. Beyond today the dominant scheduled checkpoints are Thursday's 30-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC and September CPI on 14 October.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours carry a published Claude assessment. Risk was low and mean-reverting through the Asian and early European hours of 7 October, with Tail between 10 and 14. From 11:00 to 14:00 UTC a trend-down phase lifted Tail to a 23 peak and Stress to 54 as long-end yields pushed to multi-decade highs ahead of the 10-year auction. From 15:00 UTC the mode reverted to mixed and Tail eased back to 20, 18 and then 17 as the gap-down was absorbed. Confidence held between 86 and 89 throughout.
outlookSummary: The near-term path is treated as conditionally two-way. The one named caution hour is the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where a delayed post-minutes repricing could meet cash-close imbalance; Tail is lifted to 20 for that hour only. Risk then eases through the post-close and Asian hours to a 12 trough, since thin but orderly overnight trade normally still permits retracement. Risk rebuilds gradually across the European morning on duration sensitivity, through the 12:30 UTC jobless claims release and the 13:30 UTC US cash open, and peaks at 22 for the 17:00 UTC hour containing Thursday's 30-year bond auction and a Fed speaker. Every forecast hour beyond the current one frames price-path structure conditionally; none asserts observed structure.

forecast.analysis: Observed: NDX 31,135 after a gap-down open at 30,976 and a 30,904 low, now near the 31,146 session high, so most of the decline has retraced. The 14:00 ET FOMC minutes printed with most participants expecting another hike by year-end, yet the 10-year eased to 5.28% from a 5.36% high.
